item.title: Note 10
item.description:
Notes No. 10
An average return of 0% still lost a quarter of capital. Compound rate: −13.4% a year.
A portfolio that gains 50% and then loses 50% has an arithmetic average return of 0%, yet it ends at 75 for every 100 it started with. The loss is taken on a larger base than the gain, so swings cost money even when they cancel on paper. The rate that actually describes the path is the geometric mean: the square root of 0.75, minus one, or about −13.4% a year. This gap between the two averages is called volatility drag, and it grows with the size of the swings.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
